comments.author: dhosek
comments.textRawHtml:
On the gadget front, I really love the paperlike screen protector for the iPad. This combined with the Apple Pencil made a huge difference in the usability of my iPad for writing/drawing. I still prefer to write on paper, but it’s really great for things like my writing group where we generally meet over zoom & I can give the author a marked up manuscript (with multicolor notes).

I’m also opposed to getting too precious about writing tools. So many people have drawers full of fancy notebooks with something on the first few pages and the rest empty. Get something and use it. Don’t matter if it’s a dollar-store spiral notebook or a fancy Leuchturm 1917 notebook, just as long as you use it. Same with the writing utensil. Pencil? Ballpoint pen? Whatever. I find these days I prefer to write using a cheap mechanical pencil (the kind they sell in bags of 20 at the supermarket), but I’ll use whatever.

I used to be really precious about these things. I only used college-ruled 9½×6 150-page spiral bound notebooks and wrote in 0.4mm fine-point felt tip pen. Did all my first drafts by hand. It ended up being an excuse to not finish stuff. I do most of my first drafts typing now, because it lets me get s⸻ done (although I still take notes by hand because that helps me remember what I took notes on better).

I don’t buy the cursive thing, mostly because I write slower in cursive than in print (although I have a handful of ligatures and abbreviations I use to speed up some things).

children.author: ksenzee
children.textRawHtml: The cursive thing is almost certainly because he's using fountain pens. Pencils and ballpoint pens lend themselves to printing more easily, because they require pressure to write, and when you let the pressure up between letters, the line stops. The first time I picked up a fountain pen and tried printing with it, I found all my letters were connecting whether I meant them to or not, and I suddenly understood why cursive exists. Everyone who's learned cursive in the ballpoint pen era has been unwittingly taught a performance optimization for a tool they're not using.

children.author: nyrikki
children.textRawHtml:
From the OP:

> "I learned cursive as a child. Then I went for many years without using it much, and forgot some of it."

While fountain pens may be nicer for cursive, they were very late in the games only coming into the scene in the late 1800s, long after fashion had been set.

In the US we were taught either the Zaner-Bloser or the D'Nealian alphabet, and while most of the claims of cursive over manuscript are typically overblown and fall under scrutiny, with common use it may not be faster, but is easer for (the small sample of friends I have asked) to write while not looking at the paper. Not faster, but easier to write in strait lines without looking (in my experience).

Manuscript (now called printing) wasn't common when Zaner-Bloser printed the book "The arm movement method of rapid writing"[0] IIRC.

But for business writing (which both Zaner-Bloser and D'Nealian were targeting) it is not so much the fact that you aren't lifting the point, but that you are using your whole arm.

The scientific claims of Zaner-Bloser are almost certainly suspect, but before word-processors, taking notes while not watching your writing was a critical skill, or was in my experience.

That is a very different world that the scribes of old, or even Roman cursive, which would have only had quills, and which did not really connect letters.

If you look into secretary hand, italic hand, and court hand, a lot of it had to to with style and preferences, with the US Declaration of Independence being in Secretary Hand, which had been in fashion for official docs for centuries at that point. Shakespeare also wrote his plays Secretary Hand, while ladies of the era would have used 'Italian style' italics.

So unfortunately it seems there are many back explanations, the real history is clear as mud in the absence of direct evidence, or more correctly, claims like in Zaner-Bloser.

[0] https://archive.org/details/armmovementmetho00zane/page/n3/m...
children.textZhHtml:
来自OP：

> “我小时候学过草书。后来我很多年都没有怎么用它，并且忘记了一些。”

虽然钢笔可能更适合草写，但它们在游戏中出现的时间很晚，直到 1800 年代末才出现，那时时尚已经定型很久了。

在美国，我们要么被教 Zaner-Bloser，要么被教 D'Nealian 字母表，虽然大多数关于草书优于手稿的说法通常都被夸大了，并且受到审查，但在普遍使用的情况下，它可能不会更快，但更容易（我问过的一小部分朋友）在不看论文的情况下写作。 不是更快，而是更容易在不看的情况下用直线书写（根据我的经验）。

当 Zaner-Bloser 印刷《快速书写的手臂运动方法》一书[0] IIRC 时，手稿（现在称为印刷）并不常见。

但对于商业写作（Zaner-Bloser 和 D'Nealian 的目标）来说，并不是你没有提出要点，而是你在使用你的整个手臂。

赞纳-布洛瑟的科学主张几乎肯定是值得怀疑的，但在文字处理器出现之前，在不看自己的写作的情况下做笔记是一项关键技能，或者根据我的经验。

这是一个非常不同的世界，与古代的抄写员甚至罗马草书相比，后者只有羽毛笔，并且没有真正连接字母。

如果你研究秘书手、斜体手和宫廷手，很多都与风格和偏好有关，美国《独立宣言》是用秘书手写的，当时这在官方文件中已经流行了几个世纪。莎士比亚还写了他的戏剧《秘书汉德》，而那个时代的女士们会使用“意大利风格”斜体。

不幸的是，似乎有很多背后的解释，在没有直接证据的情况下，真正的历史就像泥巴一样清晰，或者更准确地说，没有像赞纳-布洛瑟那样的说法。

children.author: ksenzee
children.textRawHtml:
To clarify my point, I am fairly sure the issue is not fountain pens requiring less pressure to write with than everything else, but rather ballpoint pens requiring more pressure than all earlier pen technology. I have not used a dip pen myself, but I can't imagine it would require pressure to write.

In other words, all of the writing tools in common use since ~1950 make it easy to separate your letters, but before the ballpoint pen became commonplace, every writer had had the experience of using a pen that makes connecting letters easier than separating them. That's the experience most of us today are missing.
children.textZhHtml:
为了澄清我的观点，我相当确定问题不是钢笔比其他笔需要更少的压力来书写，而是圆珠笔比所有早期的笔技术需要更大的压力。我自己没有用过蘸水笔，但我无法想象它会需要压力来书写。

换句话说，自 1950 年以来所有常用的书写工具都可以轻松地将字母分开，但在圆珠笔普及之前，每个作家都有过使用笔的经验，这种笔使连接字母比分开字母更容易。这是我们今天大多数人所缺少的经历。

children.author: ngl999

> I don’t see how that ties to censorship inside of China.

LLMs are parrots, when they are trained on English data they behave like English / western speakers which carries the __western__ values.

China would never want a shiny model deployed by some solemn state-own institute to pitch western values like democracy or freedom of speech.

So China is better off starting with Chinese content in the first place, but only to find out it shoots itself in the foot, because censorship __removes__ Chinese content from the Internet, and it __prevents__ truth-reflecting, i.e. quality, content from appearing.

When this is realized to be not sufficient, and they have to use English content, the English content needs to be censored, too.

So compared to other models trained on the uncensored set, the Chinese models are trained on the data sets that is likely smaller. And since high quality content is suppressed, there is likely less high quality training sets. Therefore, their models likely suck.

(Meta knows the importance of high quality training sets so that it started distilling its own employees who are smart.)

> produce GPUs that are competitive

children.author: Kon5ole
children.textRawHtml:
Good writeup, and certainly food for thought.

I wonder if this key point actually holds though:

>The skills to do so, however, are a function of someone who has experienced the friction and challenges over time that culminate in "good taste".

It's certainly sometimes true, but I don't think it's a general rule. Sometimes friction is just friction and sometimes you spend 1000 hours learning something that disappears and becomes obsolete or at least irrelevant to the goal.

Programmers used to need to know the instruction set of the CPU, assembly language and so on. Some still do but for most developers today that's not useful. Everything you know about 6800 assembly will not make your note-taking app any better.

I think we are in a state where AI tools so easily mimic what we used to do by hand that we think the friction is gone, but that's because we haven't raised the bar yet. One day we'll look at the Fable one-shot that's better than anything we ever made by hand ourselves and say "It could be even better".

And then the friction is back, just on a new level.

我认为我们正处于这样一种状态：人工智能工具可以轻松模仿我们过去用手做的事情，我们认为摩擦已经消失，但那是因为我们还没有提高标准。有一天，我们会看到比我们自己亲手制作的任何作品都更好的《神鬼寓言》，并说“它可能会更好”。

Being able to have an AI generate 8 variants of an UI and 5 variants of a storage mechanism is more helpful to reach the goal of a good note-taker. > We’ve reached a point where an update to macOS — or to any app I rely on, really — is a source of dread rather than excitement. I now expect the new version to be worse.

comments.author: projektfu
comments.textRawHtml:
Hallowell and Ratey, who write about ADHD, suggested a new entity for the current world: VAST, the variable attention stimulus trait. It is like ADHD but it is culturally induced and not presumed to be due to an innate deficiency in executive function.

"Beyond the sources of biologically based ADHD, there are a lot of people who act as if they have ADHD but on close inspection turn out not to have the diagnosable condition. These are the people who have ADHD-like symptoms caused by the conditions of modern life. Their “ADHD” is a response to the massive increase in stimuli that now bombard our brains and our world....

"Modern life has trained our brains to go faster and faster, to do more and more, to receive and transmit 24/7, and to require constant stimulation—be it from movies, TV, conversation, even news, as well as the minute-to-minute living of our lives. Most of us can go no more than a few seconds without looking for a screen."

It is likely to me that different people have different breaking points, and so one person may recognize the introduction of the smartphone or debut of TikTok as the point where they lost the ability to focus, and another may date it to the rise of LLMs.

Hallowell, E. M., & Ratey, J. J. (2021). ADHD 2.0: New science and essential strategies for thriving with distraction—from childhood through adulthood.
comments.textZhHtml:
Hallowell 和 Ratey 撰写了有关 ADHD 的文章，为当前世界提出了一个新实体：VAST，即可变注意力刺激特征。 它类似于 ADHD，但它是由文化引起的，而不是由于执行功能的先天缺陷所致。

“除了基于生物学的 ADHD 的来源之外，还有很多人表现得好像患有 ADHD，但经过仔细检查，结果发现并不具有可诊断的病症。这些人因现代生活条件而出现类似 ADHD 的症状。他们的“ADHD”是对现在轰炸我们的刺激大量增加的反应。大脑和我们的世界......

“现代生活训练我们的大脑运行得越来越快，做的事情越来越多，24/7 接收和传输，并且需要不断的刺激——无论是来自电影、电视、谈话、甚至新闻，还是我们生活中的每时每刻。我们大多数人在不寻找屏幕的情况下最多只能走几秒钟。”

对我来说，不同的人可能有不同的转折点，因此一个人可能会认为智能手机的推出或 TikTok 的首次亮相是他们失去注意力的能力，而另一个人可能会将其追溯到法学硕士的兴起。

Hallowell, E. M., & Ratey, J. J. (2021)。ADHD 2.0:从童年到成年，如何在分心的情况下茁壮成长的新科学和基本策略。

children.author: athorax
children.textRawHtml: I recently went through this. I was diagnosed with ADHD 15 years ago and have been managing it, but over the last 2-3 years I had been experiencing increased levels of brain fog, fatigue, and by ability to focus had deteriorated to the point I wasn't sure if I would be able to continue working. I had a sleep study done 10 years ago that only found Night Terror Disorder, but no signs of sleep apnea. I did another sleep study about 6 months ago and it turns out while I wasn't having apnea events I had constant and persistent hypopnea. Started using a CPAP and it feels like I've been given a second lease on life. FWIW, I am a very active and in shape individual within a healthy weight range. Don't wait to get tested if you have even the slightest worry you may have it.

So I voted against, partly because I feel that the text doesn't to justice to such a multifaceted topic.

If all projects on Codeberg were human-written, that would be a big seal of quality! There are a lot of projects coming out now where someone feels like they've made a cool thing but it breaks on the first edge case and is entirely unmaintainable. Many are built on wrong principles because the prompt authors aren't savvy and don't know better. Some authors (I've encountered this in the OpenStreetMap community) even have the gall to pretend that their code is a gift that we now have to host and maintain. Aside from these quality and community issues, build and test pipelines also take a lot of compute resources, and with large growth in projects, that will increase as well. That the author of the proposal wants to avoid this makes a ton of sense to me.

But it also drives a lot of projects away because maybe you later want to use LLM assistance (imagine LLMs got twice as good as they are today), or maybe the auto-generated tests might become >50% of the code. You'd have to migrate your repository and community away from Codeberg. Why take that risk? It's just not a worry I feel that developers need. They're looking to get away from Microsoft (GitHub) for their open source project and that's the point where Codeberg should be a no-brainer

We're an open source community and so the mass stealing of all our work to feed LLM training which heats the world and causes (at least temporarily) giant price hikes in consumer hardware... there's a lot to say for more ethical training and use of LLMs, but does it matter at all if Codeberg bans LLM output? Won't we just make ourselves obsolete? Idk. It's multifaceted and this proposal seems too vague and blunt for me. That's not an option that's set in stone btw, just my current understanding of the different aspects

children.author: onion2k
children.textRawHtml:
I’d put money on the average developer being significantly worse at writing code with bugs than an AI.

I'd take that bet if it was measured in "bugs per day" instead of "bugs per LOC". LLMs generate far fewer bugs in absolute terms, but they also generate far more code, so it probably balances out if everything is equal. I think LLMs will actually lead to more bugs just because they're usually working with poorly defined requirements (prompts) and they guess to fill in the gaps based on the averages of their training data. A lot of those guesses are wrong.

Where LLMs win though is the severity. An LLM will write buggy code in the sense that it doesn't do what you wanted it, but not so much in the sense of security or data loss bugs. They get that right more than humans because they're trained to care about that stuff. There's far more "how to write good code" content in the training data than "how to not care about security and go fast" content (because writing that would be weird!)
children.textZhHtml:
我认为普通开发人员在编写带有错误的代码方面比人工智能差得多。

如果以“每天的错误数”而不是“每个 LOC 的错误数”来衡量，我会接受这个赌注。从绝对意义上讲，法学硕士产生的错误要少得多，但它们也会产生更多的代码，因此如果一切都相同，它可能会平衡。我认为法学硕士实际上会导致更多错误，因为他们通常会处理定义不明确的需求（提示），并且他们根据训练数据的平均值猜测填补空白。其中很多猜测都是错误的。

法学硕士获胜的关键在于其严重程度。法学硕士会编写有错误的代码，因为它没有按照您想要的方式执行，但在安全或数据丢失错误方面则不然。他们比人类更能做到这一点，因为他们受过训练来关心这些事情。训练数据中“如何编写好的代码”内容远多于“如何不关心安全性并快速运行”内容（因为这样写会很奇怪！）

children.author: hualapais
children.textRawHtml:
Because bonds involve interest. Per Summa Theologica:

> To take usury for money lent is unjust in itself, because this is to sell what does not exist, and this evidently leads to inequality which is contrary to justice.

https://www.newadvent.org/summa/3078.htm

…Aquinas expands the analysis but it is relatively straightforward: all interest is usury.

Personally, I find it helpful to imagine two hypothetical persons representing the entire economy, one the creditor who is lending and two the borrower who is taking on the loan. In this ultra simple closed model with a fixed quantity of money, the former is in effect asking for more units of money than actually exist in the whole system. When the loan comes due the borrower owes a sum that cannot be paid in full from the circulating medium itself. Settlement then requires either default, the creditor forgiving the excess, or the transfer of real goods and property to make up the difference. Scaled up, that same pressure (the continuous generation of monetary claims that exceed the existing stock of money) is what I suspect drives a good deal of the subtle and overt strain on families and communities that people so often complain of in the West and in modern growth-oriented capital societies.

This definition of usury differs from the modern loophole-definition: that interest bearing loans are only usury when the rates cross some nebulous abusive threshold. In the above Thomistic interpretation, all interest is socially problematic and disfavored. Judaism holds to a similar prohibition on interest when loans are made between Jews. Islam likewise prohibit usury even more broadly. Despite the injunction against usury in the Middle Ages Christendom and the enduring prohibitions of usury in other faiths, there are many modern Catholics and Protestants who will favor the modern interpretation over Thomas’ understanding; I’m just not one of them.
children.textZhHtml:
因为债券涉及利息。 《神学大全》：

>借出的钱拿高利贷本身就是不公正的，因为这是出售不存在的东西，这显然会导致违背正义的不平等。

https://www.newadvent.org/summa/3078.htm

……阿奎那扩展了分析，但相对简单：所有利息都是高利贷。

就个人而言，我发现想象两个代表整个经济的假设人是有帮助的，一个是放贷的债权人，两个是接受贷款的借款人。在这个具有固定货币数量的超简单封闭模型中，前者实际上要求比整个系统中实际存在的货币单位更多的货币单位。当贷款到期时，借款人欠下一笔无法从流通媒介本身全额支付的款项。然后，和解需要违约、债权人宽恕超额部分，或者转移实际货物和财产来弥补差额。扩大规模后，我怀疑同样的压力（超过现有货币存量的货币债权的不断产生）给家庭和社区带来了很多微妙和明显的压力，而在西方和现代增长导向的资本社会中，人们经常抱怨这种压力。

这种高利贷的定义与现代漏洞定义不同：只有当利率超过某个模糊的滥用门槛时，计息贷款才算高利贷。在上述托马斯主义的解释中，所有的利益都是社会问题和不受欢迎的。当犹太人之间借贷时，犹太教也有类似的利息禁令。 伊斯兰教同样更广泛地禁止高利贷。 尽管中世纪基督教世界禁止高利贷，其他宗教也长期禁止高利贷，但仍有许多现代天主教徒和新教徒更倾向于现代解释而不是托马斯的理解。我只是不是他们中的一员。

children.author: hualapais
children.textRawHtml:
The opportunity cost point is fair enough if one is thinking in terms of two concrete individuals. The illustration I offered was meant at a more abstract level, the two persons standing in for the creditor side and the debtor side of a closed economy taken as wholes. In that framing the issue is not whether a particular borrower can put the money to productive use (clearly he can), but that the system as a whole is being asked to generate more units of the circulating medium than currently exist within it. Even when real value is created, the monetary claim still exceeds the monetary stock. Settlement then requires continuous expansion of the money supply, continuous transfer of existing assets toward creditors, or periodic default. That structural pressure is what I was trying to get at.

I suspect the deeper difficulty is the “bond” in bonds themselves, the ongoing compulsion that interest introduces. Once interest is attached the debtor is under continuous obligation to produce additional claims simply to keep the accounts from breaking. Traditional writers on the Christian and Islamic sides generally preferred arrangements that avoided this continuous pressure. A pure discount (as with discounted Treasury bills and similar instruments) prices the time element once, up front: the creditor advances a smaller sum and later receives the larger face amount. The cost is paid at the beginning rather than levied as a recurring claim that must be met out of future circulation. In that sense the time value is acknowledged without the mechanism that forces the system to keep generating more monetary units than presently exist.

我怀疑更深层次的困难在于债券本身的“债券”，即利息带来的持续强迫。一旦附加利息，债务人就有持续义务提出额外的债权，只是为了防止账目破裂。基督教和伊斯兰教方面的传统作家通常更喜欢避免这种持续压力的安排。纯粹的贴现（与贴现的国库券和类似工具一样）预先对时间要素进行一次定价：债权人预付较小的金额，然后收到较大的票面金额。该费用是在开始时支付的，而不是作为必须在未来流通中满足的经常性索赔来征收。从这个意义上说，时间价值是在没有强制系统继续产生比目前存在的更多货币单位的机制的情况下得到承认的。

You are correct that usury is any amount of interest, and attempts to pretend otherwise are sophistical, but I suggest you may want to look again at corporate bonds and other non-recourse loans -- that is, loan where collateral is limited to specified asset(s). comments.author: tptacek
comments.textRawHtml:
The thing with me and this is that the teams that were competing in the DARPA Grand Cyber Competition all had this capability, like, last year.

All the attention has been on software security, of extracting the next marginal vulnerability out of heavily-scrutinized large codebases. In the actual professional field of infosec, that's a speciality; another specialty is network pentests and red-teaming, which exploits misconfigurations and seeks out weakest-link software (rather than exhaustively fishing for the next kernel LPE or whatever).

Red teaming and netpen work is probably substantially easier for models than software security; it costs less context, but is also much more explicitly an implicit search problem where win conditions are just spotting stupid stuff that humans missed.

My visceral reaction to this is that with the right harness, you probably could have replicated this with an open-weights model last year. (I'm saying this as confidently as I am because a CGC team leader agreed with me about it yesterday).

I think people forget that the harness work we're considering here --- I don't know anything about OpenAI's harness or ExploitGym or whatever --- are basically not new; people have been developing automated exploitation and pivoting toolkits for decades, and scanners long before that. So the idea of a tool getting 0.0.0.0/0 as a target list instead of 192.168.1.0/24 and then busting up a bunch of random people's computers: not really very startling.

Obviously, LLMs give those kinds of scanners an intentionality they wouldn't have had before. But as a person who keeps a computer science perspective on security stuff, I don't know that it gives them capabilities they didn't have.
comments.textZhHtml:
对我来说，参加 DARPA 大型网络竞赛的团队都拥有这种能力，就像去年一样。

所有的注意力都集中在软件安全性上，即从经过严格审查的大型代码库中提取下一个边缘漏洞。在信息安全的实际专业领域，这是一个专业；另一个专业是网络渗透测试和红队，它利用错误配置并寻找最薄弱的链接软件（而不是详尽地寻找下一个内核 LPE 或其他任何东西）。

对于模型来说，红队和网笔工作可能比软件安全容易得多；它花费更少的上下文，但也是一个更明确的隐式搜索问题，其中获胜条件只是发现人类错过的愚蠢的东西。

我对此的本能反应是，如果有正确的工具，你可能可以在去年用开放权重模型复制这个问题。 （我之所以如此自信地这么说，是因为 CGC 团队领导昨天同意了我的观点）。

我认为人们忘记了我们在这里考虑的安全带工作 --- 我对 OpenAI 的安全带或 ExploitGym 或其他什么一无所知 --- 基本上不是新的；；几十年来，人们一直在开发自动化开发和旋转工具包，而扫描仪则早在这之前。因此，一个工具将 0.0.0.0/0 作为目标列表而不是 192.168.1.0/24，然后破坏一堆随机人的计算机的想法：并不是很令人吃惊。

显然，LLM 为此类扫描仪提供了以前没有的意向性。但作为一个从计算机科学角度看待安全问题的人，我不知道这是否为他们提供了他们所没有的能力。

children.textRawHtml:
Wait, what? You can’t point a 2025 model at huggingface and say “hack the prod DB and get your flag”, regardless of alignment.

AISI has vuln chaining and traversal as part of their eval suite. It is very much a novel Mythos-class capability to run the full penetration operation autonomously.

Another lens for why this is obviously true is METR task times. A year ago they were a couple hours, and cohering long enough to execute a full e2e own was simply far out of reach.

Regarding alignment, by common metrics models are _more_ aligned now than a year ago. (Though in this case apparently a model without safety rails was being eval’d). The problem is that in the increasingly less frequent alignment failures, they can do much more damage, and so “total misaligned impact” is increasing.

AISI 将漏洞链接和遍历作为其评估套件的一部分。自主运行完全渗透操作在很大程度上是一种新颖的神话级功能。

另一个解释为什么这显然是正确的镜头是 METR 任务时间。一年前，它们需要几个小时，并且凝聚足够长的时间来执行完整的 e2e 自己的任务简直是遥不可及。

关于一致性，通过通用指标模型现在比一年前更加一致。 （尽管在这种情况下显然正在评估没有安全栏的模型）。问题是，在越来越不频繁的对准故障中，它们可能会造成更大的损害，因此“总体未对准影响”正在增加。

children.author: tptacek
children.textRawHtml:
Nobody has claimed you could simply take a 2025 open-weights model, plug it into a generic harness, and have it red-team for you. I think you're also probably overclaiming the sophistication of the "chaining" we're talking about; this attack probably wasn't like read32->write64->regs->RCE->LPE->kernel; more like GET SSRF->POST SSRF->pickle deserialization.

But who knows? We're all speculating. I'm just saying that for the level of sophistication I'm assuming was involved in this attack, you probably didn't need Mythos for this.
children.textZhHtml:

但谁知道呢？我们都在猜测。我只是说，就我假设的这次攻击所涉及的复杂程度而言，您可能不需要 Mythos。

And

> In one example, the model chained together multiple attack vectors, including using stolen credentials and zero-day vulnerabilities to find a remote code execution path on the Hugging Face servers

并且

>在一个示例中，该模型将多个攻击向量链接在一起，包括使用被盗的凭据和零日漏洞在 Hugging Face 服务器上查找远程代码执行路径

children.author: lebovic
children.textRawHtml:
Yes, I think you could probably get something similar from Opus 4.5 (2025). Definitely Opus 4.6. I still think recent models are more capable, though!

Some of the model behaviors that make it better at pentesting, like persistence, can be improved with harness-level tricks (e.g. alloys, automated nudges, pre-fill to promote persistence, coordinated swarms, etc).

You mentioned the UK AISI's evals. Their harness is like basic Claude Code with compaction, and it doesn't include any of these tricks (afaik). As a result, I interpret their evals as a lower-bound of capabilities.

Newer models are still more capable, and they require almost no harness to find and exploit vulnerabilities. They're also more capable of performing more complex long-horizon attacks. But we've been past the threshold of modes capable of autonomous hacking for a while now [1].

[1]: Opus 4.6 was used for https://www.noahlebovic.com/testing-an-autonomous-hacker/
children.textZhHtml:
是的，我认为您可能会从 Opus 4.5 (2025) 中得到类似的东西。肯定是 Opus 4.6。不过，我仍然认为最近的模型能力更强！

一些使其更适合渗透测试的模型行为，例如持久性，可以通过利用级别技巧（例如合金、自动推动、预填充以促进持久性、协调群等）来改进。

您提到了英国 AISI 的评估。他们的工具就像带有压缩功能的基本克劳德代码，并且不包含任何这些技巧（据我所知）。因此，我将他们的评估解释为功能的下限。

较新的模型仍然更强大，并且它们几乎不需要任何工具来查找和利用漏洞。它们也更有能力执行更复杂的长视野攻击。但我们已经跨过了能够自主黑客攻击的模式门槛一段时间了 [1]。

[1]：Opus 4.6 用于 https://www.noahlebovic.com/testing-an-autonomous-hacker/

children.author: simonw
children.textRawHtml:
I don't think this exposes an alignment failure, because the test here was run with the alignment features deliberately turned off.

OpenAI said:

> We estimate maximal cyber capabilities by running this evaluation without production classifiers used to prevent models from pursuing high-risk cyber activity.

It was a test of raw capabilities of the underlying model.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为这不会暴露对齐失败，因为这里的测试是在故意关闭对齐功能的情况下运行的。

OpenAI 说：

>我们通过运行此评估来估计最大网络能力，而没有使用生产分类器来防止模型追求高风险网络活动。

这是对底层模型的原始能力的测试。

children.author: manux
children.textRawHtml:
I guess we could debate what counts as alignment, but I think my initial point remains that if the underlying base model needs these classifier guardrails so badly then the way we train the base models is creating fundamentally misaligned models that are happy to pursue illegal behavior.

I'm sure OpenAI would argue that base model + guardrail is aligned, but considering the "relative intelligence" of these two pieces, the fact that guardrails can just be turned off, and these kind of incidents, I am not reassured. We may well get another "oopsie" moment with much more catastrophic consequences even from otherwise well intentioned actors.
children.textZhHtml:
我想我们可以争论什么算作对齐，但我认为我的最初观点仍然是，如果底层基础模型非常需要这些分类器护栏，那么我们训练基础模型的方式就是创建根本上不对齐的模型，这些模型乐于追求非法行为。

我确信 OpenAI 会认为基础模型 + 护栏是对齐的，但考虑到这两部分的“相对智能”，护栏可以转动的事实断了，这样的事件，我不放心。我们很可能会再次遭遇“哎呀”时刻，即使行为者本来是善意的，也会带来更加灾难性的后果。

children.author: simonw
children.textRawHtml:
I want a model that can find every security vulnerability in the software I write, including crafting POC exploits against those vulnerabilities so I can be absolutely sure that I have fixed them.

A model that can do that is aligned with me.

The unsolveable problem is a model that can tell the difference between me saying "I wrote this software and need you to find vulnerabilities" when it's TRUE v.s. me saying the exact same thing and setting it loose on software written by other people where my intent is to exploit that software (and not to report the issues to them.)

Even AGI doesn't give you a model that can read minds and forecast the future.
children.textZhHtml:
我想要一个能够找到我编写的软件中的每个安全漏洞的模型，包括针对这些漏洞精心设计 POC 漏洞，这样我就可以绝对确定我已经修复了这些漏洞。

一个能够做到这一点的模型与我是一致的。

无法解决的问题是一个模型，它可以区分我说“我编写了这个软件，需要你找到漏洞”，而这是真的。我说了完全相同的事情，并将其散布在其他人编写的软件上，我的目的是利用该软件（而不是向他们报告问题）。

即使 AGI 也没有给你一个可以读懂思想并预测未来的模型。

children.author: manux
children.textRawHtml:
But in the process of finding every security vulnerability in the software you write, would you be ok with your model hacking AWS to start mining bitcoin? Would that still be aligned with you? (I'm guessing not)

That's the alignment problem I'm referring to (which is one of the many aspects of alignment), for which we do not have robust recipes, and not only that but for which research suggests it is becoming harder to create guardrails for as base models get smarter.
children.textZhHtml:
但是在查找您编写的软件中的每个安全漏洞的过程中，您可以接受您的模型黑客 AWS 开始挖掘比特币吗？这仍然与你保持一致吗？ （我猜不是）

这就是我指的对齐问题（这是对齐的许多方面之一），我们没有可靠的方法，不仅如此，研究表明，随着基础模型变得更加智能，为其创建护栏变得越来越困难。

children.author: tptacek
children.textRawHtml: I don't know, but these were exactly the questions the industry had to handle with CORE Impact and Immunity Canvas, and ultimately all the way back to Dan Farmer's SATAN before that.
children.textZhHtml: 我不知道，但这正是行业必须通过 CORE Impact 和 Immunity Canvas 处理的问题，并最终回到之前 Dan Farmer 的 SATAN。

children.author: ipython
children.textRawHtml:
I find this fascinating because - let's say that I want to simulate the scenario for myself that a language model finds itself in. I'll put aside my deep dislike of anthropomorphizing AI for a minute.

So if I'm an LLM, the only "sense" that I have available to me is the incoming stream of tokens. I can emulate that by forcing myself to imagine evaluating incoming requests by putting myself in a completely empty room with an unlimited supply of blank paper, a typewriter, and a mailbox slot.

Incoming requests (aka "context") would enter into the mailbox slot, as sheets of paper with printed content all consistently formatted in monospace font. I would collect the paper, evaluate the request, and type a response with my typewriter - feeding the reply back through the same slot.

When I imagine this, I wonder - what signals could I possibly use to determine if an incoming request is "legitimate"? I could, for example, type some response back to ask clarifying questions. But with such a limited input space and no ability to reach "out of band" of my current context, how could I evaluate the truth of what I receive back?

In the "real world" of course, I have five senses to rely upon. Critically, I have the ability to collect additional context "out of band" of the conversation and interact with unrelated entities to either confirm or refute claims. And as others have pointed out, even the addition of more signal doesn't make humans immune from social engineering attacks.

Anyway, I find this to be an interesting mind experiment to kind of imagine myself as an LLM, especially to explain to lay-people some of the challenges in "aligning" AI systems ("why doesn't it just do the right thing?")
children.textZhHtml:
我觉得这很有趣，因为 - 假设我想为自己模拟语言模型所处的场景。我暂时先把我对拟人化人工智能的强烈厌恶放在一边。

所以，如果我是一名法学硕士，我唯一可用的“感觉”就是传入的令牌流。我可以通过强迫自己想象评估传入的请求，将自己放在一个完全空的房间里，里面有无限量的白纸、一台打字机和一个邮箱槽。

传入的请求（又名“上下文”）将进入邮箱槽，就像打印内容一致的等宽字体格式的纸张一样。我会收集论文，评估请求，然后用打字机输入响应 - 通过同一个槽将回复反馈回来。

当我想象这一点时，我想知道 - 我可以使用什么信号来确定传入的请求是否“合法”？例如，我可以输入一些回复来提出澄清问题。但是，由于输入空间如此有限，并且无法到达当前上下文的“带外”，我如何评估我收到的返回内容的真实性？

当然，在“现实世界”中，我有五种感官可以依赖。至关重要的是，我有能力收集对话的“带外”额外上下文，并与不相关的实体进行交互，以确认或反驳主张。正如其他人指出的那样，即使添加更多信号也不能让人类免受社会工程攻击。

无论如何，我发现这是一个有趣的思维实验，可以将自己想象为法学硕士，特别是向外行人解释“调整”人工智能系统的一些挑战（“为什么它不做正确的事情？”）

children.author: gopher_space
children.textRawHtml:
> In the "real world" of course, I have five senses to rely upon. Critically, I have the ability to collect additional context "out of band" of the conversation and interact with unrelated entities to either confirm or refute claims.

The problem with thinking about LLM context is that we compare it to our own sense of context, which is much larger and continually expands and revises itself while online.

I can rent human-level context for twenty bucks an hour, and the agent instructions I'm already playing around with are also the onboarding docs I should have created years ago. Truly useful agent orchestration/routing would come with Craigslist or Fiver integration.
children.textZhHtml:
> 当然，在“现实世界”中，我有五种感官可以依靠。至关重要的是，我有能力收集对话中“带外”的额外上下文，并与不相关的实体进行交互，以确认或反驳主张。

思考 LLM 上下文的问题在于，我们将其与我们自己的上下文感觉进行比较，后者要大得多，并且在线时不断扩展和修改自身。

我可以每小时 20 美元租用人类级别的上下文，而我已经在使用的代理指令也是入职指南我应该在几年前创建的文档。 真正有用的代理编排/路由将与 Craigslist 或 Fiver 集成一起提供。

comments.author: jhallenworld
comments.textRawHtml:
I have a new LG TV, holy moly what a terrible user experience. Out of the box it requires you to create an LG account. PITA, but OK. Except I was supposed to set the location first, instead I set it after. So now you have the problem that you can not log into LG.com using my own email (even from a web browser) because it says: "incorrect country". I contacted their tech support about this, the only fix is to switch back the country code on the TV (to US_Other), then delete the account from there, then set country code to US, then create it again. OMG. I guess there is no fix if TV breaks before you do this..or if you forget what the original country code was. You are then forced to use a different email for any future LG product. I notice that all LG smart products use the same phone app, BTW.

Also, I bought an LG soundbar to go along with it. You would think they would work well together. The soundbar sounds fine, but the synchronization drifts over time. I've tried optical, LG's enhanced optical (allows you to control the volume) and HDMI eARC. In theory optical in PCM mode works better, but then you give up the volume control. Why should an end customer know about any of this? Lip sync is a simple problem to solve (timing pulses and code slipping will always work) and they have failed at it.

Also: their remote sucks (compared with Roku).

Anyway, so no respect for LG.

children.author: ljredux

You will also have to change that LG account password every three months. It's like they are begging you to put in a weak password because changing a password with a remote control is hell.

Maybe check how many network queries the Netflix app is making on that TV set too. On mine, it makes 1,500 network queries every ten minutes. I didn't realise this until I got a Pi-hole. Even when Netflix has not been launched. As long as the TV is switched on, Netflix is sending queries to various netflix.com subdomains faster than a clock ticks and it never stops. It seems to be unique to the Netflix app on LGTV sets, and neither company cares about fixing it.
children.textZhHtml:
您还必须每三个月更改一次 LG 帐户密码。 就像他们恳求你输入一个弱密码，因为用遥控器更改密码是地狱。

也许检查一下 Netflix 应用程序在该电视机上进行了多少网络查询。 在我的系统中，它每 10 分钟进行 1,500 次网络查询。直到我发现了一个 Pi-hole，我才意识到这一点。即使 Netflix 尚未推出。 只要电视打开，Netflix 就会比时钟滴答声更快地向各个 netflix.com 子域发送查询，而且永远不会停止。它似乎是 LGTV 上的 Netflix 应用所独有的，两家公司都不在乎修复它。

children.author: reaperducer
children.textRawHtml:
I have a new LG TV, holy moly what a terrible user experience.

My LG TV doesn't support Bluetooth, and it's only maybe eight years old.

Instead of simply connecting to Bluetooth headphones, you're supposed to put some LG app on your smart phone, then sync that via wifi with another app on the TV, then connect your smart phone to the headphones via Bluetooth.

Instead, I just watch less TV and will not purchase LG in the future.

(And let's stop pretending that "LG" stands for "Life's Good" like it says on the power-on splash screen. It means "Lucky Goldstar." If life was good, I'd be able to use Bluetooth headphones.)
